# Scope — See, update & uninstall every Linux app

Scope is a free, open-source desktop app for Linux (GUI, built with Tauri v2 + Rust + React) that unifies APT, Snap, Flatpak, and AppImage into one searchable list. Users can update or uninstall any app with preview-first, Polkit-authorized operations.

## Pages

- [Homepage](https://khurrambhutto.github.io/scope/) — Overview, screenshots, install instructions, and FAQ for the Linux app manager.
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope) — Source code, issues, and releases.
- [Releases](https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope/releases) — Pre-built .deb, AppImage, and .rpm packages for x86_64 Linux.

## Key Information

- **Current version**: 0.1.8
- **License**: MIT
- **Stack**: Tauri v2, Rust backend, React + TypeScript frontend
- **Platform**: Linux (x86_64) — Ubuntu/Debian (.deb) primary, plus AppImage and .rpm
- **Author**: Khurram Bhutto (https://khurrambhutto.github.io/portfolio-site/)
- **Features**: Unified package list across APT/Snap/Flatpak/AppImage, real-time search, source filters, preview-first update/uninstall plans, protected-package deny-list, Polkit (pkexec) privilege escalation, background task center with logs

## Installation

Ubuntu / Debian:

```bash
sudo apt install ./Scope_0.1.8_amd64.deb
```

Or download the AppImage or .rpm from https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope/releases/latest

From source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope
cd scope
npm install
npm run tauri dev
```

## FAQ

**What is Scope?**
A Linux desktop app that scans APT, Snap, Flatpak, and AppImage into a single searchable list, with safe preview-first updates and uninstalls.

**Which package managers are supported?**
APT/dpkg (manual packages), Snap (runtime/base snaps hidden), Flatpak (user and system scopes), and AppImage files in ~/Applications and ~/.local/bin.

**Is it safe to uninstall apps with Scope?**
Yes — every operation shows a preview plan first, a backend deny-list blocks removal of system-critical packages, and privileged operations go through Polkit (pkexec) so Scope never handles passwords.

**Is it free?**
Yes, MIT-licensed open source software.
